claim: A federal statute expressly preempting, or imposing a moratorium on, state laws that regulate AI models or systems generally is signed into law before the 119th Congress ends on January 3, 2027.
claim_es: Una ley federal que de forma expresa desplace (preempción) las leyes estatales que regulan modelos o sistemas de IA en general, o les imponga una moratoria, se promulga antes de que el 119.º Congreso termine el 3 de enero de 2027.
falsifier: No such statute signed by Jan 3, 2027. Does NOT count: executive orders (including EO 14365), agency rules or FCC/FTC actions, court rulings, discussion drafts, bills passing one chamber only, or sector-specific preemption (e.g., child online safety or privacy bills) that does not reach state AI laws generally.
falsifier_es: No se promulga ninguna ley de ese tipo antes del 3 de enero de 2027. NO cuentan: órdenes ejecutivas (incluida la EO 14365), reglamentos de agencias o actuaciones de la FCC o la FTC, fallos judiciales, borradores de discusión, proyectos aprobados por una sola cámara, ni el desplazamiento sectorial (por ejemplo, leyes de seguridad infantil en línea o de privacidad) que no alcance a las leyes estatales de IA en general.
resolution_source: Congress.gov public law record, confirmed by at least one of Nextgov, Politico, StateScoop, or TechPolicy.Press.
notes: Sources: EO 14365 (Dec 11, 2025); Ropes & Gray 2026-03-11 (OBBBA 99-1 vote, FY26 NDAA omission); Nextgov 2026-06-04 (Obernolte–Trahan discussion draft, 3-year preemption); CASRAI status check 2026-09-20 (draft still unintroduced, organized state and labor opposition). Tests enactment, not merits. Conflict flag: see positions record.
reference_class: Congressional attempts to preempt state AI laws via standalone or must-pass bills, 2025–26 (Senate stripped the OBBBA moratorium 99-1; omitted from the FY2026 NDAA); adjusted for the Obernolte–Trahan draft remaining unintroduced as of Sep 2026 and a lame-duck FY2027 NDAA as the remaining vehicle.
reference_class_es: Intentos del Congreso de desplazar las leyes estatales de IA mediante proyectos independientes o de trámite obligado, 2025–26 (el Senado eliminó la moratoria de la OBBBA por 99 a 1; se omitió de la NDAA del ejercicio 2026); ajustado porque el borrador Obernolte–Trahan seguía sin presentarse en septiembre de 2026 y porque la NDAA del ejercicio 2027 en sesión saliente es el vehículo restante.

claim: The Department of Defense, the Office of Golden Dome for America, or U.S. Northern Command publicly declares initial operational capability (or an explicitly equivalent 'initial capability operational' status) for the Golden Dome homeland missile defense architecture on or before December 31, 2028.
claim_es: El Departamento de Defensa, la oficina de Golden Dome for America o el Mando Norte de Estados Unidos declara públicamente la capacidad operativa inicial (o un estado explícitamente equivalente de “capacidad inicial operativa”) para la arquitectura de defensa antimisiles del territorio nacional Golden Dome, el 31 de diciembre de 2028 o antes.
falsifier: No official declaration of IOC or explicit equivalent for the Golden Dome architecture as a whole by Dec 31, 2028. Does NOT count: activation of individual operational sites (including Fort Story, VA, announced Aug 2026), component tests, demonstrations, contract awards, or relabeling of existing systems without an architecture-level declaration.
falsifier_es: No existe declaración oficial de capacidad operativa inicial, ni equivalente explícito, para la arquitectura Golden Dome en su conjunto antes del 31 de diciembre de 2028. NO cuentan: la activación de sitios operativos individuales (incluido Fort Story, Virginia, anunciado en agosto de 2026), pruebas de componentes, demostraciones, adjudicaciones de contratos, ni el cambio de nombre de sistemas existentes sin una declaración a nivel de arquitectura.
resolution_source: Official DoD, Golden Dome office, or NORTHCOM release or on-record statement by the Golden Dome director or NORTHCOM commander, confirmed by at least one of SpaceNews, Breaking Defense, Defense News, or Aviation Week. Declaration date governs.
notes: Tests declaration, not effectiveness. Guetlein's two-stage plan: stitch existing systems into an initial shield by 2028, purpose-built affordable architecture by 2035. Sources: SpaceNews (Erwin) 2026-09-21; CRS IF13264 2026-07-08 ($185B through 2035 per Guetlein, CBO $1.2T over 20 years, Fort Story site Aug 2026); National Defense Magazine 2026-04-10 (Harrison skepticism on 2028 deliveries). Conflict flag: see positions record.
reference_class: Major DoD programs with politically fixed IOC dates; adjusted up because Phase 1 integrates systems already in production and the declaration is administrative, adjusted down for interceptor delivery lead times and program-office delays through 2026.
reference_class_es: Programas mayores del Departamento de Defensa con fechas de capacidad operativa inicial fijadas políticamente; ajustado al alza porque la Fase 1 integra sistemas que ya están en producción y la declaración es administrativa, y a la baja por los plazos de entrega de los interceptores y los retrasos de la oficina del programa a lo largo de 2026.

claim: NASA's Space Reactor-1 Freedom (or a renamed successor that is NASA's fission-powered nuclear electric propulsion spacecraft to Mars) lifts off on or before December 31, 2028.
claim_es: El Space Reactor-1 Freedom de la NASA (o un sucesor renombrado que sea la nave de propulsión eléctrica nuclear por fisión de la NASA con destino a Marte) despega el 31 de diciembre de 2028 o antes.
falsifier: No liftoff with the reactor aboard by Dec 31, 2028. A launch without the reactor, a descoped non-nuclear mission, or a slip to the 2031 Mars window resolves false. Reactor startup after launch is not required.
falsifier_es: No hay despegue con el reactor a bordo antes del 31 de diciembre de 2028. Un lanzamiento sin el reactor, una misión reducida sin componente nuclear, o un aplazamiento a la ventana marciana de 2031 lo resuelven como falso. No se exige que el reactor arranque después del lanzamiento.
resolution_source: NASA launch release, confirmed by at least one of SpaceNews, Ars Technica, NASASpaceflight, or SpacePolicyOnline. Liftoff date (UTC) governs.
notes: Announced March 2026 under NASA's Ignition initiative: ~20 kWe reactor powering the repurposed Gateway Power and Propulsion Element, carrying the Skyfall helicopters. Cost estimate $2.1B excluding helicopters (Ars Technica 2026-09-01; verify against the primary article before publishing). Sources: ANS Nuclear Newswire 2026-03-25; MIT Technology Review 2026-04-14; SpacePolicyOnline on the OSTP Space Nuclear Initiative. Conflict flag: see positions record.
reference_class: NASA first-of-kind technology demonstrations tied to fixed planetary launch windows; adjusted down for the first U.S. space reactor since SNAP-10A (1965) with the reactor as the primary new system, adjusted up for scope limited to existing hardware (repurposed Gateway PPE).
reference_class_es: Demostraciones tecnológicas primeras en su tipo de la NASA atadas a ventanas de lanzamiento planetarias fijas; ajustado a la baja por tratarse del primer reactor espacial estadounidense desde el SNAP-10A (1965), con el reactor como el principal sistema nuevo, y al alza porque el alcance se limita a hardware existente (el Power and Propulsion Element de Gateway reutilizado).

claim: A nuclear thermal propulsion engine built by or for a U.S. government agency or U.S. company operates in space, with the reactor critical and heated propellant producing thrust, on or before December 31, 2032.
claim_es: Un motor de propulsión nuclear térmica (nuclear thermal propulsion) construido por o para una agencia del gobierno de Estados Unidos o una empresa estadounidense opera en el espacio, con el reactor en estado crítico y propelente calentado que produce empuje, el 31 de diciembre de 2032 o antes.
falsifier: No public confirmation of an in-space nuclear thermal engine firing by Dec 31, 2032. Does NOT count: ground tests, nuclear electric propulsion (including SR-1 Freedom), surface or orbital power reactors, or a launch in which the engine never fires.
falsifier_es: No hay confirmación pública de que un motor de propulsión nuclear térmica haya encendido en el espacio antes del 31 de diciembre de 2032. NO cuentan: pruebas en tierra, propulsión eléctrica nuclear (incluido el SR-1 Freedom), reactores de potencia en superficie o en órbita, ni un lanzamiento en el que el motor nunca encienda.
resolution_source: Official agency or company release, confirmed by at least one of SpaceNews, Ars Technica, or Breaking Defense. Firing date governs.
notes: DARPA canceled DRACO in 2025, citing falling launch costs eroding the ROI of nuclear thermal R&D; NASA's FY2026 request zeroed NTP and NEP funding. Sources: SpaceNews 2025-07-02; Nuclear Engineering International 2025-07-08. Paired with Entry A: space nuclear power vs. nuclear rockets. Conflict flag: see positions record.
reference_class: U.S. space nuclear propulsion programs 1955–2025 (Rover/NERVA, SP-100, Timberwind, Prometheus, DRACO, JETSON): none reached flight. Adjusted for current federal momentum directed to nuclear electric propulsion and surface power rather than nuclear thermal.
reference_class_es: Programas estadounidenses de propulsión nuclear espacial, 1955–2025 (Rover/NERVA, SP-100, Timberwind, Prometheus, DRACO, JETSON): ninguno llegó a volar. Ajustado por el impulso federal actual, dirigido a la propulsión eléctrica nuclear y a la potencia en superficie antes que a la propulsión nuclear térmica.

reference_class: DOE-authorized reactor startups under the 2025-26 pilot and authorization pathway, time from facility arrival to criticality; adjusted for Radiant's missed July 4 target and Aug 25 DOME arrival.
claim: Radiant's Kaleidos microreactor achieves zero-power criticality at INL's DOME facility on or before September 30, 2026.
falsifier: No public confirmation by Radiant, INL, or DOE that criticality occurred on or before Sep 30, 2026.
resolution_source: Radiant, INL, or DOE announcement stating the criticality date. An announcement published through Oct 7 counts if it dates criticality on or before Sep 30.
notes:
Context: Szumowski (@UnoMasReactor) post 2026-09-20 implying imminent criticality after ~1 month of Radiant silence. Conflict flag: see positions record.

EVIDENCE. DOE selected Radiant's Kaleidos in July 2025 for the first fueled experiment in INL's DOME test bed, as early as spring 2026 (energy.gov). World Nuclear News, 2026-08-18, reported Kaleidos shipped to Idaho with the campaign targeted to complete in Q3 2026 on TRISO fuel from Standard Nuclear. Radiant's own X post of 2026-08-25 announced arrival at DOME. The LA Business Journal, 2026-08-31, reported Kaleidos had not yet achieved criticality. Kevin's note records a missed 4 July criticality target. As of 2026-09-20 no public confirmation of criticality exists, roughly 26 days after arrival. The Szumowski signal is third-party, not a company or DOE statement.

BASE RATE. Two comparable DOE pilot startups reached criticality in 2026: Antares' Mark-0 on 4 June at INL and Valar's Ward 250 on 18 June. Neither arrival-to-criticality interval is established from a fetched source, so the population is named but not measured. First-of-a-kind nuclear programmes miss stated dates far more often than they hit them, and Radiant has already missed one.

CASE HIGHER. The hardware is on site and fueled operations are the remaining step. A knowledgeable third party is signalling imminence. The federal fiscal year ends 30 September, which is a real forcing function for a DOE pilot demonstration.

CASE LOWER. Ten days is a narrow window for a first-of-a-kind authorization-to-operate sequence. A month of company silence more often indicates a hold than a surprise. The one prior stated date was missed. Authorization is DOE's to give, not Radiant's to take.

SUGGESTED RANGE 0.30-0.45. Toward the top on a DOE or INL authorization notice before 25 September; toward the bottom if silence continues past 25 September.

KEY UNCERTAINTY. Whether DOE has already issued the authorization to operate. That one fact would collapse the range.

WEAKNESS. Two of the three named resolution sources (Radiant, and to a degree INL) have a stake in the outcome. Claim text drafted 2026-09-20, commit f921551; probability set 2026-09-21.
claim_es: El microrreactor Kaleidos de Radiant alcanza criticidad a potencia cero en la instalación DOME del INL el 30 de septiembre de 2026 o antes.
falsifier_es: No hay confirmación pública por parte de Radiant, el INL o el DOE de que la criticidad haya ocurrido el 30 de septiembre de 2026 o antes.
reference_class_es: Arranques de reactores autorizados por el DOE bajo la vía piloto y de autorización de 2025-26, medidos como el tiempo entre la llegada a la instalación y la criticidad; ajustado por el objetivo incumplido del 4 de julio de Radiant y por su llegada al DOME el 25 de agosto.

claim: Radiant completes all five phases of its Kaleidos DOME test campaign, including the 150-hour continuous run without operator intervention, on or before December 31, 2026.
claim_es: Radiant completa las cinco fases de su campaña de pruebas Kaleidos en el DOME, incluida la corrida continua de 150 horas sin intervención de operadores, el 31 de diciembre de 2026 o antes.
falsifier: No public confirmation that the 150-hour continuous run finished on or before Dec 31, 2026.
falsifier_es: No hay confirmación pública de que la corrida continua de 150 horas haya terminado el 31 de diciembre de 2026 o antes.
resolution_source: Radiant, INL, or DOE announcement stating the 150-hour run completion date. An announcement published through Jan 7, 2027 counts if it dates completion on or before Dec 31, 2026; completion date governs, not announcement date.
notes:
Sources: Radiant blog 'Kaleidos Has Left the Building' (five-phase plan, criticality framed as basic physics only); World Nuclear News 2026-08-18; Interesting Engineering 2026-08-19 (Q3 completion target); Radiant X post 2026-08-25 (DOME arrival). Conflict flag: see positions record.

EVIDENCE. Radiant's own campaign description sets out five phases and frames criticality as the basic-physics step rather than the end. Interesting Engineering, 2026-08-19, reported a Q3 2026 completion target, and Q3 ends 30 September. The fifth phase includes a 150-hour continuous run without operator intervention, which is 6.25 days of wall clock and cannot start later than about 24 September. As of 2026-09-20 criticality is not publicly confirmed, so the whole remaining sequence — criticality, power ascension through the intermediate phases, then the continuous run — has ten days.

METHOD NOTE (Kevin, 2026-09-20): MC, not RC. This is arithmetic on a fixed-duration run against a fixed deadline, not a base rate over a population. The comparison below is context, not the method.

CONTEXT. First-of-a-kind power ascension runs weeks to months from first criticality to sustained full power. No fetched source establishes a shorter precedent for this class of machine.

CASE HIGHER. Q3 is the company's own stated target and companies sometimes compress to hit a quarter. The phases may overlap rather than run strictly serially. The run may already have begun without announcement.

CASE LOWER. The arithmetic is unforgiving. Criticality is unconfirmed on 20 September, so every intermediate phase would have to clear in under four days combined, with no hold points, on a machine that has already missed a date.

SUGGESTED RANGE 0.03-0.10. Toward the top only on confirmation that criticality occurred before 22 September.

KEY UNCERTAINTY. Whether the five phases are serial or overlapping, and whether the 150-hour run requires full rated power or a lower hold point.

WEAKNESS. The claim is compound (all five phases) while the falsifier tests only the fifth. See the run report. REVISED 2026-09-21: the Sep 30 version of this claim was not logged. It failed the short-horizon rule in register/README.md, which admits a claim resolving inside 90 days only with a range of 0.20-0.80, and its honest range was 0.03-0.10. The resolution date moved to Dec 31, 2026 and the method moved from MC to RC. The suggested range recorded above belongs to the Sep 30 claim and does not apply to this one. Claim text drafted 2026-09-20, commit f921551; probability set 2026-09-21.
reference_class: First-of-a-kind reactor power ascension schedules; adjusted for a stated Q3 2026 target, a missed July 4 criticality target, and one quarter of slip allowance.
reference_class_es: Cronogramas de ascenso de potencia de reactores primeros en su tipo; ajustado por un objetivo declarado para el tercer trimestre de 2026, un objetivo de criticidad incumplido el 4 de julio y un trimestre de margen por retraso.
